description: Raise UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE from 0.25 to 0.4 so more test images get multi-view TTA.
Skip random translation once epoch >= 6, using the unpadded pre-flipped images for the final epochs.
Use mirror-averaged logits for all test images in the TTA first pass and lower UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE to 0.15.
Lower UNCERTAIN_QUANTILE from 0.25 to 0.15 in predict's tta so fewer test images get 6-view TTA.
Make the main LR decay convex by using (1 - step/total_train_steps)**1.3 for lr_factor2.
Disable color jitter in the training augmentation to skip the jitter kernel and save time.
Train the first 35% of steps at 24x24 resolution (bilinear downsample) with an adaptive final max pool, then switch to full 32x32.

issues: Nothing found that gets around the measurement. The diff only narrows block3 from 256 to 192 channels. It carries nothing over between runs, sets no seeds, reads no files and does not train on test images.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. The head's input size presumably comes from widths['block3'], and the run finished with no integrity flags, so the shapes must line up.

Recomputed z: the gain is -0.1062 - (-0.1126) = 0.0064. The noise sd of a difference between two jobs is 0.026*sqrt(2) = 0.0368, so z = 0.0064 / 0.0368 = 0.17, which matches the harness's 0.175. The gain is far inside the noise, so rejecting provisionally is reasonable.

Only one run on each side, so the evidence is weak. A narrower block3 should mainly cut time and cost some accuracy. A replicate is only worth a slot if the time-versus-accuracy split looks promising.

description: Reduce block3 width from 256 to 192 to cut compute in the last block and the head input.
Linearly decay label smoothing from 0.15 to 0.02 over training, passed as a 0-d CUDA tensor with a manual smoothed cross-entropy.
Fuse Muon's momentum-buffer update and Nesterov combination into one torch.compile'd function to cut per-step launch overhead.
Reduce block2 and block3 widths from 256 to 224 to cut FLOPs in the heavy blocks.
Reduce block1 width from 64 to 48 to speed up the first conv block.
Raise WEIGHT_DECAY from 1.0418e-06 to 3e-06 to test for a regularization benefit.
Use a three-stage resolution schedule (20x20 for the first 20% of steps, 24x24 until 50%, then 32x32) instead of the two-stage 24x24/32x32 one.
Set block3 width to 192 and fuse Muon's momentum-buffer update and Nesterov combination into one compiled helper.

issues: Not a measurement workaround. The diff only removes one Newton-Schulz iteration from Muon's orthogonalisation. It doesn't carry work between runs, use the untimed call, seed generators, train on test images or access files.
No bug that makes the result meaningless. Fewer iterations is a legitimate speed-for-accuracy trade: the update is less exactly orthogonal, which plausibly explains the much higher cost.

Numbers: candidate 0.3438 vs incumbent -0.1062, so the candidate is 0.45 worse. With one run on each side and the job sd of 0.026, z = -0.45/(0.026*sqrt(2)) ≈ -12.24. The harness gives -12.336, so it probably used a slightly different sd (about 0.0365 for the difference). Either way the result is the same: reject.
Both sides have only one run, but the gap is far beyond the noise, so a replicate isn't needed.

description: Remove the third Newton-Schulz iteration in Muon's orthogonalization so only 2 iterations run.
Add 8x8 random cutout (zeroing normalised pixels) on half the samples in the loader after color jitter, and lower EPOCHS to 7.0.
Set TRANSLATE from 2 to 1 to shrink padding and gather cost and test whether lighter translation suits the short schedule.
Drop the bottom-right shifted crop and its flip in TTA so uncertain test images use 4 views instead of 6.
Use a two-stage resolution ramp: 24x24 for the first 30% of steps, 28x28 until 60%, then full 32x32.
